text: I just learned that 80%, 80% of organ donors are women, 80% of organ recipients are men. So men don't want to be organ donors, but they want, they want the organs that are being donated. They don't, they don't want to help other people, but they want to be helped. Of course, hypocrisy at its finest. This is completely and utterly wrong. And this is a prime example of how quickly and widely misinformation can spread. This video got 2.6 million views and more than 650,000 likes. Now let's look at the actual data. According to the Global Observatory on Donation and Transplantation, the GODT, around 60-65% of organ recipients are men, not 80% like she claimed. And around 60-65% of organ donors are men too. So her claim that 80% of donors are women is simply wrong and not supported by global data. And for those wondering whether this source is reliable, the GODT is widely described as the most comprehensive global database on donation and transplantation. It is a collaborative effort of the World Health Organization and Spain's Organización Nacional de Transplantes, and it is based on official national sources. Now I do want to point out one thing before someone else writes it. It is true that around 60% of living donors are women, but most organ transplants come from diseased donors. Only around 20% of transplants come from living donors, while around 80% of transplants come from diseased donors. So I feel it is important to point this out. However, those who want to say, the girl in the video only meant kidney or liver donations and only in the state of Pennsylvania, well, then she should be more specific in her video. It is not my job to guess what exactly she meant. She made a broad claim, and that claim was completely wrong. For other people, please do not believe everything you hear online. Use critical thinking and double-check the information, including information coming from me, as I can make mistakes too.
